source_question: Based on the above information, is the following statement true, false, or uncertain? Zayn does not care about the environment.
formalization_prompt:
Read this logical world and question. Write ordinary SWI-Prolog source that you believe helps test one relevant hypothesis, plus one bare callable Prolog query to execute. The query is an API argument, not a console command: never include ?- or a trailing period. You may use normal facts, rules, helper predicates, and built-ins; do not call the shell, read files, use network, or add directives. This is an exploratory diagnostic, not a request for a final A/B/C answer.

Trusted Prolog capabilities can be inspected live with meta_signatures(Signatures) and meta_help(all, Documentation). Known callable signatures include audit_trace/2; audit_proof_tree/2; labelled_explanation/3; labelled_semantic_status/3; semantic_status/3; semantic_slice_status/3; finite_status/6; finite_sat_status/5. audit_proof_tree/2 returns a nested dependency tree only for a successful forward-Horn derivation; it never fabricates a proof for XOR, disjunction, negation, or quantifiers. Formulas accepted by the semantic helpers: atom(Name, Args), not(F), and(F,G), or(F,G), xor(F,G), implies(F,G), forall(var(Name,Type),F), exists(var(Name,Type),F). Explicit quantifier example: domain(person,[ada]). axiom(s1,forall(var(x,person),implies(calm(var(x)),ready(var(x))))). In the body, var(x) references the bound variable; x or 'X' alone is a constant. Every var(Name) reference must have an enclosing matching quantifier. Ordinary rule([calm(X)],ready(X)) implicitly quantifies its Prolog variable over person. Vacuous quantifiers and constants matching binder names are legal and reported by quantifier_audit; inspect their source text before changing them. Ordinary Prolog predicates may also be defined by your own source. This is a non-scoring executor-capability probe. Do not answer the English A/B/C question. Write a complete ordinary labelled Prolog formalization: every source sentence exactly once, with an s-ID and its exact English in a preceding Prolog comment. Declare all named entities in domain(person,...). Every source sentence MUST be an axiom/2 declaration. Do not write bare facts, normal Prolog clauses, sentence/2, person_member/1, or other helper predicates. Required fact form: axiom(s2, has_serpent_body(selah)). Required ordinary Horn rule form: axiom(s3, rule([has_wings(selah), has_serpent_body(selah)], rules_the_ocean(selah))). For complex non-Horn sentences use their labelled surface directly, such as axiom(s4, implies(...)), axiom(s5, not(...)), axiom(s6, or(...)), axiom(s7, xor(...)), or axiom(s8, and(...)). Preserve not/or/xor/and rather than deleting difficult sentences. Critical requirement: the source sentence whose ordinary Horn conclusion is `enjoy_hiking(zayn)` MUST use axiom(sN, rule([Premise,...], enjoy_hiking(zayn))), never implies(...), even if you use implies for other sentences. Your bare query must be exactly audit_proof_tree(enjoy_hiking(zayn), Result), with no ?- and no trailing period. This query asks only for the stated Horn subclaim `Zayn enjoys hiking.`, not for the English question. Do not use atom(Name,Args), directives, shell, files, network, semantic_status/3, labelled_explanation/3, finite_status/6, or finite_sat_status/5. Return JSON only: {"program":"...","query":"..."}. Return JSON only: {"program":"...","query":"..."}.

World:
If Zayn appreciates scenery, then he either visits mountains or enjoys hiking. Anyone who studies ecology either protects wildlife or loves nature (or both). Anyone who has curiosity and appreciates biodiversity can study ecology. If Zayn values sustainability, then he conducts research and earns an environmental degree. If Zayn teaches others, then he either protects wildlife or preserves habitats (or both). Zayn values sustainability. If Sweetness enjoys hiking, then he works outdoors. Saanvi supports conservation. Andi values sustainability. Sweetness lives in a rural area. If Andi works outdoors, then he either supports conservation or protects wildlife, but not both. If Zayn lives in a rural area, then he will likely enjoy hiking. If Sweetness values sustainability, then he conducts research and earns an environmental degree. Anyone who earns an environmental degree will study ecology. Zayn conducts research. Andi conducts research. Zayn lives in a rural area. If Zayn enjoys hiking, then he works outdoors. If Zayn is a volunteer, then he either works outdoors or teaches science, but not both. If Zayn works outdoors, then he either supports conservation or protects wildlife, but not both. Zayn supports conservation.

Question:
Based on the above information, is the following statement true, false, or uncertain? Zayn does not care about the environment.

formalization.program:
% Named entities in the world.
axiom(s0, domain(person, [zayn, sweetness, saanvi, andi])).

% If Zayn appreciates scenery, then he either visits mountains or enjoys hiking.
axiom(s1, implies(appreciates_scenery(zayn), or(visits_mountains(zayn), enjoys_hiking(zayn)))).

% Anyone who studies ecology either protects wildlife or loves nature (or both).
axiom(s2, forall(var(x, person), implies(studies_ecology(var(x)), or(protects_wildlife(var(x)), loves_nature(var(x)))))).

% Anyone who has curiosity and appreciates biodiversity can study ecology.
axiom(s3, forall(var(x, person), implies(and(has_curiosity(var(x)), appreciates_biodiversity(var(x))), studies_ecology(var(x))))).

% If Zayn values sustainability, then he conducts research and earns an environmental degree.
axiom(s4, implies(values_sustainability(zayn), and(conducts_research(zayn), earns_environmental_degree(zayn)))).

% If Zayn teaches others, then he either protects wildlife or preserves habitats (or both).
axiom(s5, implies(teaches_others(zayn), or(protects_wildlife(zayn), preserves_habitats(zayn)))).

% Zayn values sustainability.
axiom(s6, values_sustainability(zayn)).

% If Sweetness enjoys hiking, then he works outdoors.
axiom(s7, implies(enjoys_hiking(sweetness), works_outdoors(sweetness))).

% Saanvi supports conservation.
axiom(s8, supports_conservation(saanvi)).

% Andi values sustainability.
axiom(s9, values_sustainability(andi)).

% Sweetness lives in a rural area.
axiom(s10, lives_in_rural_area(sweetness)).

% If Andi works outdoors, then he either supports conservation or protects wildlife, but not both.
axiom(s11, implies(works_outdoors(andi), xor(supports_conservation(andi), protects_wildlife(andi)))).

% If Zayn lives in a rural area, then he will likely enjoy hiking.
axiom(s12, rule([lives_in_rural_area(zayn)], enjoy_hiking(zayn))).

% If Sweetness values sustainability, then he conducts research and earns an environmental degree.
axiom(s13, implies(values_sustainability(sweetness), and(conducts_research(sweetness), earns_environmental_degree(sweetness)))).

% Anyone who earns an environmental degree will study ecology.
axiom(s14, forall(var(x, person), implies(earns_environmental_degree(var(x)), studies_ecology(var(x))))).

% Zayn conducts research.
axiom(s15, conducts_research(zayn)).

% Andi conducts research.
axiom(s16, conducts_research(andi)).

% Zayn lives in a rural area.
axiom(s17, lives_in_rural_area(zayn)).

% If Zayn enjoys hiking, then he works outdoors.
axiom(s18, implies(enjoys_hiking(zayn), works_outdoors(zayn))).

% If Zayn is a volunteer, then he either works outdoors or teaches science, but not both.
axiom(s19, implies(is_volunteer(zayn), xor(works_outdoors(zayn), teaches_science(zayn)))).

% If Zayn works outdoors, then he either supports conservation or protects wildlife, but not both.
axiom(s20, implies(works_outdoors(zayn), xor(supports_conservation(zayn), protects_wildlife(zayn)))).

% Zayn supports conservation.
axiom(s21, supports_conservation(zayn)).
